title: Eye & brain
examples: How does my eye change focus when I look at things far away?
Which part of the brain is responsible for interpreting what my eyes see?
What happens to the lens when I look at a close book?

explain.say: The eye has several important parts that work together.
The cornea is the transparent outer layer at the front of the eye.
The lens changes shape to focus light onto the back of the eye.
Accommodation is the process of adjusting the lens focus.
The brain processes the signals sent from the retina via the optic nerve.
When you look at a distant object, your lens flattens out.

faq.q: How does the eye actually focus light onto the retina?
faq.a: The lens changes its shape, a process called accommodation. This changes how much light is bent before it hits the light-sensitive retina.

faq.q: What is the role of the brain in vision?
faq.a: The brain receives electrical signals from the optic nerve. It then interprets these raw signals into the recognizable images we see.
asks: Does the eye see things or does the brain see things?
How does the brain process what I see?

faq.a: Accommodation is necessary because the distance of an object changes the amount of light entering the eye. The lens adjusts to keep the focus sharp.
asks: Why does my eye change focus?

faq.a: The optic nerve is the cable that carries electrical signals from the retina back to the brain. It is the pathway for visual information.
asks: Where do the signals go after the retina?
What connects the eye to the brain?

faq.q: Is the cornea the same as the lens?
faq.a: No, the cornea is the fixed outer window, while the lens is the adjustable structure behind it. Both help bend the light entering the eye.
asks: Which part bends the light the most?
Are the cornea and lens different?

facts: The cornea provides most of the eye's focusing power.
The retina contains photoreceptor cells that detect light.
Accommodation allows the eye to focus on objects at different distances.
The optic nerve transmits visual information to the brain.

quiz.say: If you look at a very close book, the lens will:
quiz.why: A thicker lens bends the light more strongly, which is needed to focus on nearby objects.

wrong.1: This would happen when looking at something very far away.
wrong.2: The lens must change shape to keep the focus clear.
wrong.3: Transparency is always maintained by the eye structure.

quiz.say: The signals leaving the eye travel along which structure?
quiz.why: The optic nerve is the dedicated pathway that carries the electrical impulses from the retina to the brain.

wrong.0: The cornea is a physical part of the eye, not a signal cable.
wrong.1: The lens changes light, but it does not carry the signal.
wrong.2: The retina captures the light, but the nerve carries the signal away.

quiz.say: Which brain region processes the raw visual data?
quiz.why: The visual cortex, located in the brain, is the area specialized for interpreting visual information.

wrong.0: The hypothalamus controls body temperature and hormones.
wrong.2: The cerebellum controls balance and body movement, not sight.
wrong.3: The brainstem controls basic life functions like breathing.
